title: As Jacob With Travel Was Weary
print: The engraving SDAHImages 628.png (github.com/adventHymnals/SDAHImages, docs/seventh-day-adventist-hymnal/SDAHimages/628.png), read line by line on 2026-10-18. Four systems: bars 1-3, 4-6, 7-11 and 12-17, as the engraving numbers them. The stanzas are lyric rows 1., 2. and 3. under systems 1 to 3; the refrain, marked Refrain, starts at the double bar in system 3 (its first line in row 2) and ends at the final barline. hymnal.db stored stanza 2 as one run-together line ("passo'er") and stanza 1's first word as "A". Each line is as the engraving prints it, its syllables joined, its punctuation kept (its curly quotation marks written as straight ones, as the row writes them).

stanzas.text: As Jacob with travel was weary one day,
At night on a stone for a pillow he lay;
He saw in a vision a ladder so high
That its foot was on earth and its top in the sky.
Come let us ascend! all may climb it who will;
For the angels of Jacob are guarding it still:
And remember each step that by faith we pass o'er,
Some prophet or martyr has trod it before.
And when we arrive at the haven of rest
We shall hear the glad words, "Come up hither, ye blest,
Here are regions of light, here are mansions of bliss."
O who would not climb such a ladder as this?

lines.text: Alleluia to Jesus who died on the tree,
And has raised up a ladder of mercy for me,
And has raised up a ladder of mercy for me.
